original_question: Is it consistent that the club principle ♣_{ℵ1} holds and at the same time the strong polarized relation \( inom{\omega_1}{\omega} 	o  inom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.21 in §3: “Is it consistent that ♣_{ℵ1} holds and \binom{\omega_1}{\omega} \to \binom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2?” ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem asked in the paper: the consistency of the club principle ♣_{ℵ1} together with the positive strong polarized relation at the pair (\omega_1,\omega). ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: It should say explicitly that the consistency question is over ZFC.

It should unpack the polarized-arrow notation using Definition 1.1: for every coloring c: \omega_1 \times \omega \to 2, there exist A \subseteq \omega_1 and B \subseteq \omega with |A|=\omega_1 and |B|=\omega such that c restricted to A \times B is constant. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
It should make explicit that this is the positive strong polarized relation with 2 colors, not a weaker or asymmetric variant. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

For full paper-faithful context, it should note that any positive answer must also have ¬CH, because Theorem 2.1 gives the negative relation under CH and the paper states this consequence immediately after Problem 3.21. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the club principle ♣_{ℵ1} holds and, simultaneously, every coloring c: \omega_1 \times \omega \to 2 admits sets A \subseteq \omega_1 and B \subseteq \omega with |A|=\omega_1 and |B|=\omega such that c is constant on A \times B; equivalently, that \binom{\omega_1}{\omega} \to \binom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since CH implies \binom{\omega_1}{\omega} \not\to \binom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 by Theorem 2.1, one may ask whether ZFC + ♣_{ℵ1} + ¬CH + \binom{\omega_1}{\omega} \to \binom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 is consistent. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially Problem 3.21 verbatim. The only paper-critical additions needed to make it fully stand-alone are the formal expansion of the strong polarized relation from Definition 1.1 and the nearby observation that a positive answer must negate CH, via Theorem 2.1 and the remark immediately following Problem 3.21. This keeps the scope exactly on the first-infinite-cardinal case treated in §3, without drifting to neighboring questions about weak diamond, other cardinal invariants, or uncountable κ. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
